caption: The drawing depicts a wall with geometric and architectural elements rendered primarily in shades of red, blue, gray, and brown. The focal point is a rectangular niche or doorway with a darkened interior, framed by an arched decorative border with a small cross at the top center and red and blue ornamental designs. Surrounding the niche are two thick red columns with blue capitals, supporting wide arches. These arches feature a repeating pattern of red segments alternating with blue designs that resemble hanging decorations. To the left of the niche, there is a circular motif containing a small red diamond shape and a line extending downward, ending in a triangular section and an angular bracket shape. The lower part of the wall displays alternating red and pale squares arranged in a diamond-checkerboard pattern. There is a horizontal band consisting of connected red semicircular forms outlined in blue running along the wall above the checkered section. The floor in the foreground is depicted with red-brown square tiles arranged diagonally. The overall composition uses a watercolor technique with visible blending and soft edges. The name "Harry Mann Waddell" is written in small text in the lower right corner of the image.
title: Wall Painting and Baptismal Niche
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
